physics_notes:
# Refrigerator mechanism and physics audit

This is a force-tested **simulation hypothesis**, built on `../../assets/fridge/refrigerator`. The source appliance has not been identified by model number, weighed, or tested with a force gauge. Dimensions are depth-derived metric estimates; component masses, hinge resistance and switch parameters are explicitly assumed. Passing these tests establishes the stated simulation behavior, not sim-to-real accuracy on this kitchen appliance.

The delivered standalone model is `mjcf/refrigerator.xml`, with relative `meshes/` and `textures/` assets. It requires MuJoCo 3.5 and **no callback or position controller**. Reset with `mj_resetDataKeyframe(model, data, model.key("rest").id)`; then call `mj_forward` and `mj_step`. The rest controls are `[1, 0, 1, 0]`: main magnet, main cam, freezer magnet, freezer cam. Keep the two magnet controls at 1. Cam bias forces operate independently of their zero controls. A plain `mj_resetData` resets adhesion controls to zero and is not the specified resting configuration.

All named simulation objects have the `refrigerator_` prefix. The explicitly requested keyframe is named `rest`. The cabinet is anchored; the model does not simulate appliance rolling or tipping. There are 17 scalar DOFs: 2 doors, 5 bin lifts, 3 shelves, 3 drawers, 1 dairy/upper flap, 2 thermostat knobs and 1 light plunger.

## Measurements and scale

`params.py:PARAMS` is the authoritative parameter dictionary. Its `geometry` entry imports the immutable source snapshot in `evidence/source_model.json`; all OBJ coordinates are in that same baseline metre frame. `length_scale` multiplies mesh vertices, pivots, sites, added hardware, prismatic travels, contents dimensions and switch spring reference once. `python build.py --scale 0.95` regenerates a scaled asset; `--unloaded` removes the documented contents. Masses remain product priors rather than scaling as solid volumes, and geometric inertia scales as length squared. Re-run tests and re-tune force parameters after accepting a new scale. Test thresholds in the delivered suite describe the baseline scale 1.0.

The asset frame is the **complete rest visual envelope bottom centre**, +Z up, +X right, -Y front. Its WORLD mapping is the original yaw +90 degrees and translation (-0.611468, 0.870000, 0) m. Preserving this origin also preserves the cabinet's small +Y offset of 0.0685321 m. The fixed cabinet is 0.900 x 0.720 x 1.855 m; the complete original rest envelope including handles is 0.900 x 0.857064 x 1.855 m.

The source layout's own metadata says the scale is supplied depth scale, **not a tape measurement**. Reported depth uncertainty is approximately 4%, before occlusion and pose errors. Source door fit residuals are 14.5 cm main and 8.3 cm freezer. These residuals are much larger than the numerical contact penetration tolerances and must not be confused with them. The original constrained door pivots are retained exactly:

| Door | WORLD pivot (m) | Asset pivot (m) | Axis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main | -0.23098, 1.30937, 0.62961 | 0.4393701, -0.3804879, 0.6296100 | +Z |
| Freezer | -0.25700, 1.26110, 1.56577 | 0.3911001, -0.3544679, 1.5657700 | +Z |

A fresh `ktools point f5126 297 1390` check returned WORLD (-0.4614404, 0.5829651, 0.3849048) m, consistent with the 0.380 m lower-shelf reference. Existing multi-frame shelf z samples span 0.918–0.966, 0.678–0.720 and 0.375–0.385 m. Original evidence is retained in `evidence/source_measurements.json`; measured deli extensions are 0.0855 m at f5395 and 0.205 m at f5411. Full 0.4 m deli travel is the supplied constrained-joint limit, not an observed full extension.

As a **size and total-mass comparator**, GE's GTS22KGNRBB specification gives W 32.75 in, D 34.5 in, H 66.375 in = 0.83185 x 0.87630 x 1.685925 m, with 202 lb net mass = 91.62566 kg. The source model is about 8.2% wider and 10.0% taller, while full depth is about 2.2% less. It is not defensible to identify this appliance as that GE model or silently impose an isotropic product-size correction. The scale-calibration job must resolve that discrepancy. [GE dimensions](https://products.geappliances.com/appliance/gea-pdf/GTS22KGNRBB), [GE product/net weight](https://www.geappliances.com/appliance/GE-21-9-Cu-Ft-Garage-Ready-Top-Freezer-Refrigerator-GTS22KGNRBB).

## Geometry changes and contacts

The supplied Blender geometry, convex walls and measured hinge placements are reused. Visuals retain separate enamel, ABS liner, glass, polystyrene, gasket and handle materials. Enamel, control-label and freezer-photo textures come from the source asset. MuJoCo uses simplified transparency/specular appearance; its renderer does not reproduce Blender transmission, roughness/bump maps or the original alpha-composited decal appearance. The freezer photo is displayed as a rectangular textured panel, retaining some source illumination. The original Blender file remains available for full PBR appearance.

Five previously fixed door bins now have independent upward prismatic joints, 0–0.040 m. Gravity seats them at the lower stop. These joints represent lifting out of locating rails; they do not become free bodies after the upper stop. Shelf sliders represent guided extraction, not carrying a detached shelf. Rail supports and roller bearings are ideal prismatic constraints with dissipative resistance; they are not rolling-element contact simulations. The covered compartment's observed cover is the **same upper/dairy flap**, parented to the main door. No second unsupported flap is invented.

Parent collision filtering is disabled so cupboard/door and flap/compartment interference is actually tested. This exposed two defects in the old collision model:

- The dairy flap overlapped both cheeks by approximately 4.5 mm. Its contact width is reduced by 12 mm overall and its unobserved tilted hinge axis is replaced by the horizontal door-width direction (0.998104, -0.06155, 0), normalized by MuJoCo. Its existing visible cover silhouette is retained; the collision inset represents clearance behind the outer overlapping lip. This axis correction is an engineering hypothesis, not a re-measurement.
- A small freezer-door/cabinet-edge graze near 0.0856 rad blocked force-driven opening. The freezer outer-skin collision width receives an additional 8 mm total inset, on top of the source model's 12 mm total inset. The visual envelope and constrained hinge stay unchanged. This clearance compensates incompatible independently fitted surfaces; it must be revisited after scale/shape calibration.

All 67 inherited collision pieces remain individually convex and watertight. Cabinet, drawers and bins are assembled from separate walls, retaining open cavities. A single convex hull is never substituted for an entire hollow bin or cabinet. The shell/handle pieces are physical contacts; material meshes are visual-only (group 2, collision masks zero), while convex contacts are group 3. There are no exclusions hiding the corrected flap overlap.

Each door has one dedicated rigid gasket child and a fixed striker, representing the **resultant of the distributed magnetic seal**. The 3 mm sphere pad and 12 x 8 x 25 mm striker half-extents are reduced contact geometry, not measured seal cross sections. The pad is 25 mm toward the latch edge from the handle in X, and 46 mm behind the skin centre in Y; these are inferred mounting/resultant locations. Each explicit pair only involves its own seal. The actuator targets the gasket body, so handles, door skins, bins and food cannot acquire accidental adhesion. These local mounting blocks stand in for a full continuous gasket frame and its deformation.

Contact friction is (sliding, torsional, rolling): general 0.4, 0.005 m, 0.0001 m; handle 0.8, 0.005 m, 0.0001 m; seal 0.8, 0.002 m, 0.0001 m. These are dry ABS/glass and rubber/grip engineering assumptions, not measurements. All solid contacts use `condim=3`; only sliding friction is active at that dimensionality, so torsional/rolling values are recorded for future higher-dimensional contact models. The switch pair uses `condim=1`, with no tangential resistance. Roller resistance is modeled by joint friction and damping rather than contact rolling friction.

Contact `solref` = (0.0025, 1) s/ratio, `solimp` = (0.95, 0.99, 0.001), margin = gap = 0 m. This gives contact-only adhesion with no attraction at positive separation. The contact time constant was tightened after a 50 g cavity drop exceeded 2 mm penetration at impact; the final tests include that drop. Constraint softness is a numerical calibration, not a measured rubber modulus.

## Mass and inertia

The 91.62566 kg dry total is a real product comparator, not this refrigerator's measured weight. Its allocation is assumed: 13 kg main insulated door, 7 kg freezer door; 0.35 kg per bin; 0.6 kg deli drawer; 0.9 kg per crisper; 0.16 kg flap; 0.18 kg compartment; 0.03 kg per knob; 0.012 kg switch. The cabinet receives the remainder, including an unmodeled compressor's mass. No published separate door or drawer weight was located; those values must not be described as product measurements.

Each shelf is corrected from the original 1.5 kg guess to width x depth x assumed 4 mm glass thickness x 2500 kg/m³ + 0.25 kg trim. The density is published by [Pilkington ATS-129](https://www.pilkington.com/-/media/pilkington/site-content/usa/window-manufacturers/technical-bulletins/ats-129---properties-of-soda-lime-silica-float-glass.pdf); thickness, trim and the full-area glass approximation remain assumptions. Composite door/drawer masses take precedence over volume-density estimates.

Default contents are 1.5, 2.0, 2.5 kg in the main bins; 0.5 and 0.75 kg in the freezer bins; 1 kg in the deli drawer; 2 kg in each crisper. They model plausible bottles/food, not item counts or masses inferred from photos. Contents are a rigid inertial lump with the bin footprint and 60 mm height, centred 60 mm above the source bottom centre. No hidden content collision boxes fill the cavities. Additional simulated food bodies must replace these inertial contents to avoid double-counting mass.

Inertias are integrated from each convex piece at uniform effective density within a link, then combined with the parallel-axis theorem. This uses actual wall/handle geometry rather than a link bounding box. Contents use a box inertia and their offset COM. It still assumes a mass distribution: insulation/steel layering, compressor location and uneven bottles are unmeasured. MuJoCo diagonalizes the exported full inertia tensor; armatures below are added separately. Fixed seal/striker bodies are massless parts of the door/cabinet idealization.

## Joints, spring forces and stops

Prismatic units: frictionloss N, damping N s/m, armature kg, stiffness N/m, springref m. Revolute units: frictionloss N m, damping N m s/rad, armature kg m², stiffness N m/rad, springref rad. Zero values are intentional. Armatures represent small unmodeled hinge/roller inertias and numerical regularization; they are not identified motor inertias. All joints use soft limits and friction constraints, not servos.

| Default class | frictionloss | damping | armature | stiffness | springref | Justification |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| refrigerator_door | 0.25 | 2.2 | 0.006 | 0 | 0 | assumed lubricated hinge resistance; cam is separate |
| refrigerator_drawer | 3 | 9 | 0.02 | 0 | 0 | assumed low roller drag, includes 3 N breakaway resistance |
| refrigerator_shelf | 8 | 12 | 0.02 | 0 | 0 | assumed higher sliding trim/rail resistance than rollers |
| refrigerator_bin | 0.8 | 4 | 0.005 | 0 | 0 | light clip/rail resistance; gravity seats bin |
| refrigerator_flap | 0.015 | 0.025 | 2e-05 | 0.04 | 0 | light plastic hinge with weak return spring |
| refrigerator_knob | 0.012 | 0.01 | 1e-05 | 0 | 0 | light thermostat dial resistance, no invented detents |
| refrigerator_plunger | 0.12 | 1.2 | 0.0005 | 180 | -0.003 | small spring switch with 0.54 N preload |

All joint limits use `solreflimit=(0.006,1)` and `solimplimit=(0.95,0.99,0.001)` except the plunger's stiffer end stop, `(0.002,1)` and `(0.98,0.999,0.001)`. Joint friction constraints use `solreffriction=(0.004,1)` and `solimpfriction=(0.95,0.99,0.001)`. Remaining MuJoCo impedance defaults are midpoint 0.5, power 2. These time constants and impedances are assumed compliance/stability choices. Limits constitute the end stops; no duplicated stop boxes are hidden in the geometry. Under impact, a soft stop can temporarily exceed its range slightly.

| Deli drawer | -0.0951699, -0.9937600, -0.0582400 | 0–0.400 m | supplied measured direction/range; only 0.205 m seen |
| Left/right crispers | 0, -1, 0 | 0–0.370 m | inferred independent sliders from two visible fronts |
| Glass shelves 01/02/03 | 0, -1, 0 | 0–0.450 m | extraction hypothesis, not observed removal |
| Main bins 01/02/03; freezer bins 01/02 | 0, 0, 1 | 0–0.040 m | requested lift-removal approximation; no observed unhooking |
| Upper/dairy flap | 0.998104, -0.06155, 0 | 0–1.500 rad | physically corrected horizontal axis; inferred motion |
| Thermostat knobs 1/2 | 0, -1, 0 | -2.2–2.2 rad | inherited visual affordance; not actuated in capture |

GE documents real refrigerator closing cams ([component reference](https://www.geappliances.com/appliance/Door-closing-cam-top-cam-under-refrigerator-or-freezer-door-WR2X4901)), but does not establish this unit's torque curve. The native general actuator implements a **passive cam surrogate**:

`tau_cam(q) = clamp(-T + (T/a) q, -T, 0)`

with a = 0.2094395102 rad (12°), T = 2.0 N m main and 1.8 N m freezer. Both overcome the 0.25 N m hinge friction when released anywhere up to 10°; torque rolls to zero at 12°. The conservative potential for 0≤q≤a is `T*q - T*q²/(2*a)`, then constant `T*a/2`. This equals a small cam lift energy (about 0.209 J main, 0.188 J freezer); it does not physically raise the door. Damping/friction remove energy. The cam acts as a specified effective preload, so loading changes inertia without automatically increasing cam torque. A true gravity cam would also change torque with load and is a remaining identification improvement. The built-in MuJoCo energy sensor excludes this actuator potential; the energy-decay test runs above 12°, where the cam potential is constant.

A [Toshiba refrigerator patent, JP4444330B2](https://patents.google.com/patent/JP4444330B2/en) describes approximately 30 N to peel a magnetic gasket and about 50 N with increased adhesion. That example concerns a translating freezer closure; it supplies a published gasket-force prior, not a measured swing-door value for this unit. The selected ~41 N handle thresholds lie within the user's 25–60 N range. The model does not reproduce that patent's finite peeling-distance curve, seal aging, thermal suction or time-dependent air pressure.

MuJoCo adhesion gain is **total contact force**, distributed among a target body's contacts, not a torque or per-contact gain. [MuJoCo 3.5 adhesion reference](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.5.0/XMLreference.html#actuator-adhesion). Main gain = 39 N; freezer gain = 37 N. The lever ratios, cam, hinge drag and spring-switch reaction determine the actual handle release, which is tested rather than equated to those gains. Above the seal contact, adhesion produces no generalized force even though its nominal actuator-force field remains nonzero at ctrl=1. No equality constraint or angle-triggered latch release is used in the MJCF.

Main: pad XYZ = (-0.3383802, -0.2768096, 0.9925) m; handle XYZ = (-0.3133802, -0.3961856, 0.9925) m; pad lever 0.7777502 m, handle lever 0.7527502 m.

Freezer: pad XYZ = (-0.3478317, -0.2416581, 1.5375) m; handle XYZ = (-0.3228317, -0.3538851, 1.5375) m; pad lever 0.7389318 m, handle lever 0.7139318 m.

The switch is a 12 g, 6 mm-radius spherical plunger at asset (-0.30,-0.245,1.13) m, springref -0.003 m and stiffness 180 N/m. The relaxed stop has 0.54 N spring preload. The 0.008 m upper limit supplies a second, stiff stage, not an invented electrical snap detent. A door-mounted pusher with half-extents (0.014,0.008,0.014) m produces a nominal 6 mm depression at qdoor=0. Its Y centre is `plunger_y + 0.006 - 0.006 - 0.008` m; its X/Z coincide with the tip. This exact contact placement is a modeled mechanism, not observed hardware. `refrigerator_light_switch_position >= 0.004 m` means electrically pressed/light off. This sensor rule changes only the proposed light state, never the mechanics. No electrical network is simulated.

## Automated validation

Run from this folder with a Python environment containing MuJoCo 3.5, NumPy, trimesh, Pillow and torch:

```sh
python build.py
python tests/test_physics.py
python tests/test_build.py
python tests/test_isaac.py
MUJOCO_GL=egl python render_review.py
python write_physics.py
```

`export_visuals.py` is only needed to regenerate the bundled per-material meshes from the supplied Blender asset: `blender -b -P export_visuals.py`. Ordinary MJCF loading and physics tests need no Blender and no access to the source folder. The generated model does not reference absolute machine paths.

Tests apply point forces with `xfrc_applied`: a world force at the handle and the equivalent COM torque `(handle_position - body_COM) × force`. They do not misuse a COM force as a handle force. Position initialization sets up independent trials; the actual motion is force-driven, without position actuators or writing qpos during simulation. Door forces follow the door's local outward normal. Drawer forces follow the slider axis; bin lift force includes loaded weight. Tests check finite states, engine warnings and every reported dynamic contact on every step. Numerical limit overshoot is checked separately from contact penetration.

Breakaway is bracketed to 0.126953 N by independent constant-force trials: settle 0.4 s, pull for 1 s, count release when angle >0.03 rad. This is an operational simulated threshold, not a quasi-static gauge measurement. Magnet-off control trials establish that the seal, not hinge friction, supplies most resistance. At 0.4 rad the model's magnetic/cam generalized torque is zero. The 55 N / 0.25 s pulse tests report force-driven release angles and subsequent coasting, not spring-powered pop-open or cross-compartment pressure effects.

**Final result: 12/12 MuJoCo tests passed**, 31.191 s measured wall time for 163.800 simulated seconds (includes repeated load/compile, Python monitoring and trials). This is offline test throughput, not online estimation latency. Peak monitored contact penetration = **1.3418 mm**, below 2 mm. No NaN or engine warnings occurred. Dense geometry checks cover 201 samples per joint with other doors open for access; force-driven tests also check trajectories and closed-door obstruction. This is not exhaustive proof for arbitrary simultaneous motions.

This is kinetic decay outside the cam region, not a claim that the engine includes actuator potentials. Loaded main/freezer doors accelerate more slowly under identical handle pulses; exact comparisons, dt=0.5/1/2 ms opening checks and closed-door drawer obstruction are saved in `tests/results.json`.

Five 50 g, 15 mm-radius sphere drops verify freezer floor, glass shelf, deli cavity and both crisper cavities. The 67 convex solids pass watertightness/convexity/positive-volume checks. ## Isaac Lab equivalent and remaining limitations

`isaac/actuators.py` provides `RefrigeratorActuatorCfg`, a custom `ActuatorBase` implementation and a pure torch law, targeting the [Isaac Lab 2.2.0 actuator API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/v2.2.0/source/isaaclab/isaaclab/actuators/actuator_cfg.py). `make_actuator_cfgs()` binds all 17 prefixed joints. Set imported USD masses, inertia and limits from the manifest and enable self collision; remove inherited position drives. Environment code must feed filtered gasket/striker contact booleans before every physics step. Each boolean is consumed and cleared, so stale contact cannot keep the door latched. The additional 0.02 rad angle gate prevents an erroneous far-open contact from activating the seal. Missing contact input gives zero magnetic effort.

The explicit law uses the same cam, joint stiffness/reference, damping and armature values. MuJoCo's dimensional `frictionloss` is approximated by `-F*tanh(velocity/epsilon)`; it is **not copied into PhysX's dimensionless friction coefficient**. Native friction and drive stiffness/damping are zero to avoid double counting; the custom actuator adds damping once. Velocity epsilon is 0.002 rad/s for hinges and 0.0002 m/s for sliders. PhysX stop surrogates use 10000 N m/rad for hinges and 100000 N/m for sliders, with outward-only damping 20 N m s/rad and 100 N s/m. These are explicit approximation parameters, not a mathematical conversion of MuJoCo `solref`. Imported native limits also need validation to avoid excess combined stop stiffness. The effort cap is 1000 N or N m and velocity cap 100 m/s or rad/s: loose numerical ceilings, not appliance ratings. Use 1 ms or smaller timesteps.

Two build tests verify standalone relocation, prefixed names, zero rest penetration, and 0.9x scaling of body/site positions, prismatic travel and inertia with unchanged mass (`tests/build_results.json`). Three torch tests check contact gating, the plunger's stiff second stage and dissipation. **Isaac Lab/PhysX is not installed and no Isaac simulation is claimed.** The regularized friction can creep near rest; PhysX contact gating and stop compliance need an engine-specific force test before calling it equivalent in behavior.

Remaining sim-to-real work: identify the appliance, establish tape/fiducial metric scale, weigh removable parts/door loads, measure handle pull versus separation and delay after closure, identify closing cam torque and damping, and measure bin unhooking/rail travel and switch preload. The model omits thermal suction, pneumatic coupling between compartments, magnetic-field variation at a gap, gasket peeling/deformation, structural flex, food motion, electrical/thermal operation and free carrying after removal. Hinge-axis and collision adjustments remain model assumptions with source evidence preserved.

No new capture was made. The source asset already supplies synchronized source-frame/camera/trajectory/observation replay at `../../assets/fridge/refrigerator/replay/index.html` and `reconstruction_replay.mp4`; its documented interval is f4974–f6963, 165.800–232.100 source seconds. This work adds offline simulation and synthetic review poses, not a new reconstruction or real-time estimator. No online tracking rate or sim-to-real error is measured.
